facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is built as operating loss plus depreciation and amortization; it was a loss of USD 710 million in the first nine months of 2025 and USD 613 million in the first nine months of 2026. The improvement is real but the figure stays negative because stock-based compensation of USD 855 million is expensed. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which adds that expense back, rose to USD 389 million from USD 122 million, which is why adjusted leverage fell from 8.08x at FY2025 to 2.58x on a last-twelve-months basis; leverage on reported EBITDA is not meaningful in any period. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation K1; calculation K5

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is liquidity: cash and investments of USD 6,238 million are more than six times debt, the only sizeable maturity is the USD 1,000 million 2030 notes, and free cash flow of USD 1,254 million in nine months is positive, which points to a small refinancing need before 2030 whatever the EBITDA definition. The view that earnings cover is weak would be overturned if reported EBITDA turned positive, which needs operating profit to absorb the USD 855 million of stock-based compensation expensed in the nine months, or if bookings regained growth. It would be confirmed if bookings keep falling, third-quarter bookings being USD 225 million below a year earlier, and the quarterly change in deferred revenue stays near USD 136 million, which would cut operating cash flow and leave settlement and repurchase outflows to be met from the investment portfolio. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Voting control rests with the founder alone, so no outside holder can force a change of policy and a takeover is improbable. Class B stock carries 20 votes a share and is wholly owned by the founder and his affiliates; on share counts it was 56.94% of all votes at 2026-09-30, down from 58.74% at 2025-12-31 after the number of Class B shares fell in April 2026 for reasons the filings do not give. The company has elected out of Nevada's statute on business combinations with large holders, so its defences are the dual-class structure, a staggered board and a two-thirds vote for certain charter amendments. The notes' offer to repurchase at 101% of principal on a change of control therefore protects against an event the structure makes unlikely, and gives no check on the founder's own policy choices. Class B stock carries 20 votes a share and is wholly owned by the founder and his affiliates; on share counts it was 56.94% of all votes at 2026-09-30, down from 58.74% at 2025-12-31 after the number of Class B shares fell in April 2026 for reasons the filings do not give. The company has elected out of Nevada's statute on business combinations with large holders, so its defences are the dual-class structure, a staggered board and a two-thirds vote for certain charter amendments. The notes' offer to repurchase at 101% of principal on a change of control therefore protects against an event the structure makes unlikely, and gives no check on the founder's own policy choices.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern about financial policy is that nothing in the record yet shows creditors losing from it: no controlling sponsor is named, no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases took 42.92% of nine-month operating cash flow, cash and investments of USD 6.2 billion are well above the USD 1,000 million of notes, the company states compliance with its covenants, and no amendment, waiver or exchange is described. The view would soften further if the indenture proved to restrict distributions tightly. It would harden if repurchases ran above operating cash flow or above the USD 1.0 billion first-year intention, if any distribution were debt-funded, if new debt or liens were put in place under the USD 4.0 billion basket, if settlement costs rose well above USD 140 million, or if bookings kept falling from the USD 1,697 million of the third quarter while buybacks continued. facts.text: No debt was issued, repaid or refinanced by Roblox Corporation in 2026; the nine-month cash flow statement shows no debt proceeds or repayments. facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that distress is implausible for years on the numbers reported: revenue rose 28.97% in nine months 2026, the operating loss narrowed to 17.98% of revenue from 25.12%, adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.68% from 3.51%, free cash flow of USD 1,254 million exceeded repurchases and settlements together, capital expenditure was only 1.85% of revenue, and nine-month bookings were still 9.15% higher. The view would improve if bookings returned to growth and paying users recovered, and it would worsen if bookings fell again in the fourth quarter, the strongest seasonal quarter, with deferred revenue growth below USD 136 million, if repurchases exceeded free cash flow, if settlements rose well above USD 140 million, or if any distribution were debt-funded. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Roblox runs a single-segment immersive gaming and creation platform made of a client application, a free creation toolset and cloud infrastructure. Creators build experiences and users buy the virtual currency Robux to enhance them, either one-time or through the Premium subscription. Users on the platform averaged 138 million a day in the third quarter of 2026, of whom about 1.8 million paid, and 54% of nine-month revenue came from the United States, with 57% from the United States and Canada, 21% from Europe, 12% from Asia-Pacific and 10% from the rest of the world. Creators earned USD 1,503.1 million of Developer Exchange payouts in FY2025 against USD 922.8 million in FY2024, and more than 45,000 creators were registered in the program at 2026-09-30 against more than 35,500 at 2025-12-31.

facts.text: Roblox is a listed, founder-led and founder-controlled company with no sponsor named: the founder and his affiliates own all Class B stock, which carries 20 votes a share and was 56.94% of all votes at 2026-09-30 on share counts, down from 58.74% at 2025-12-31. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is transactional and discretionary, with a subscription element, concentrated in channel and title, and sensitive to regulation. The company sets the creator payout rate in its sole discretion and has used that power to give value back: it raised the payout per earned Robux by 8.5% in September 2025 and the Developer Exchange rate by 42% for eligible adult US spend in June 2026, and it offers more Robux through lower-fee payment channels, so pricing power over creators and payers is limited and used defensively. The credit mechanism is that bookings, not revenue, drive cash; revenue is smoothed by deferral, durable items were 90% of virtual item revenue in nine months 2026, and the deferred balance gives revenue visibility of about twelve months, with USD 4,781 million of it classified as current and a tail to roughly 27 months. Users play for free, only about 1.30% of daily users pay, and the company has raised creator payouts twice, in September 2025 and June 2026, which indicates that creator retention has a cost; the mechanism is cost creep in developer exchange fees and a bookings base that depends on a small payer group. Supplier power is meaningful: Apple and Google take up to 30% of purchases on 44% of FY2025 revenue and can change terms, hosting providers hold USD 845 million of commitments, and payment processors set fees that the company manages through differential pricing. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because scale in creators and infrastructure and trust and safety spending of 24% of revenue raise the cost of entry, while the threat of substitutes is high because the same child and teen time can go to other entertainment. facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver and are covered here; economic, social and technological factors matter only where they connect to the same mechanism. Regulatory: the 2025 annual report lists the Digital Services Act, the UK Online Safety Act, Australia's minimum-age law, the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act amendments with a compliance date of 2026-04-22, state app-store and minor-purchase laws, and a possible loss of liability protections; compliance has already required mandatory age checks that, by the company's own account, led to an unexpected decline in the rate of growth. Social: the user base includes many children, so safety is a condition of the business, and it has produced state lawsuits and settlements costing USD 140 million in nine months 2026. Economic: the company cites inflation and weaker consumer spending as risks to discretionary spending by users, which reaches bookings. Technological: dependence on operating systems and app stores, and investment in age-check and moderation technology, raise cost and constrain growth. The credit effect is that regulation can change the user base and the cost base at the same time, a change that earnings cannot absorb but liquidity can. facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths in credit terms are liquidity of USD 6,238 million against debt of USD 1,009 million, advance payments and a USD 7,040 million deferred balance, low capital intensity, and a creator network whose registered Developer Exchange creators grew 26.76% in nine months. Weaknesses are negative reported EBITDA, a thin payer base, a cost base that is rising ahead of bookings, and concentration of channel and titles. The only opportunities that could improve credit quality are a return of bookings growth as users adapt to age checks, higher engagement among older audiences through the company's novel-game expansion, and lower payment costs from a mix shift to cheaper channels. The threats that could weaken credit quality are further regulatory action and fines, more state settlements, a change in app-store terms, and repurchases that outpace cash flow. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: The company states no outlook figure, so the next twelve to twenty-four months are read from reported trends. The fourth quarter is seasonally the strongest for bookings, so it is the next test of whether the third-quarter fall was a step or a trend; the company says it expects to continue safety changes in response to regulation, that safety changes have impacted and may continue to impact bookings, that it intends up to USD 1.0 billion of repurchases in the first twelve months of the program, and that settlement talks with other states continue. Company-specific tailwinds are lower payment costs from channel mix, an expanding creator base and the revenue release from the deferred balance; headwinds are age-check friction, litigation, rising hosting and personnel costs, and app-store fees. Over three to five years the 2030 maturity is the only debt event, and its repayment depends on liquidity that is currently several times debt rather than on earnings. Sector tailwinds and headwinds are not evidenced beyond the company's own risk factors and no peer data is supplied. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most credible issuer-specific downside begins with a regulatory or enforcement event that removes more users or payers than the age-check change did, such as a finding under the Digital Services Act, an action by the Federal Trade Commission, or a further wave of state measures. The first operational break is a second consecutive fall in bookings: third-quarter bookings of USD 1,697 million were USD 136 million above the USD 1,561 million at which deferred revenue would stop growing at the third-quarter revenue level, so a further fall of 8.01% would end the float. Financial transmission follows in order: operating cash flow loses the deferred revenue inflow, which was USD 533 million in nine months 2026; revenue keeps rising for several quarters from the USD 7,040 million deferred balance, so reported margins stay flattered; costs of USD 1,855 million in the third quarter, hosting commitments and legal settlements do not fall; and free cash flow shrinks from USD 364 million in the quarter toward zero.

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The liquidity and refinancing consequence is limited in the near term: on an indicative basis bookings of USD 1,441 million, 15.09% below the third quarter, would leave cash operating costs just covered before working capital, and even at zero operating cash flow cash and investments of USD 6,238 million would cover the identified fixed calls of USD 1,981 million more than three times. Management levers are suspending the repurchase program, which may be suspended at any time and has USD 2.4 billion of authority left, slowing hiring and infrastructure, and stopping further buybacks before any borrowing. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over twelve to twenty-four months; the observable triggers are a second quarter of falling bookings, a quarterly deferred revenue change below USD 136 million, free cash flow below USD 364 million, settlement expense above USD 140 million, and repurchases above free cash flow. No default is assumed. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Roblox presents a business profile that is large and broad by geography but concentrated by channel, title and paying users, supported by liquidity of USD 6,238 million and advance payments, but credit quality is constrained by negative reported EBITDA, a falling bookings and payer base, open-ended legal and regulatory cost, and policy set by one holder. Cash-flow durability appears adequate while bookings hold and weak if they keep falling, because free cash flow leans on working capital. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on liquidity, which is several times the debt, not on market access, which the filings do not evidence. The primary downside path is regulation-driven loss of paying users that cuts bookings, ends the deferred revenue float and leaves a rising cost base and legal cost to be met from the cash cushion over several years. Further analysis would require a management outlook, the indenture, ratings and market prices, peer financials and fourth-quarter results. Top risk: loss of paying users and bookings from user-safety regulation. ## Request

The five Roblox filings support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work through the quarter ended 30 September 2026, but they cannot support covenant, ratings, peer or market-price work.

# Financial foundation: Roblox Corp (rblx-1315098)
## Request

Financial foundation for Roblox Corp (Roblox Corporation, ticker RBLX; issuer id rblx-1315098), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The module puts the five supplied filings on one basis (US dollars in millions), builds net debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and debt maturity tables, and states every gap. It takes its scope from the Source readiness module and uses no other document.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Roblox's reported EBITDA is negative in every period, so leverage on reported earnings cannot be stated, and creditors rest on USD 6,238 million of cash and investments against USD 1,009 million of total debt at 2026-09-30.

On the issuer's adjusted measure, which adds back stock-based compensation, total debt is 2.58x adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months and 8.08x for FY2025. Bookings fell to USD 1,697 million in the third quarter from USD 1,922 million a year earlier, the only 2026 quarter in which bookings fell year on year, which matters because advance payments fund operating cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 148–149; calculation K1; calculation K5
### Key findings

Leverage. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is built as operating loss plus depreciation and amortization; it was a loss of USD 710 million in the first nine months of 2025 and USD 613 million in the first nine months of 2026. The improvement is real but the figure stays negative because stock-based compensation of USD 855 million is expensed. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which adds that expense back, rose to USD 389 million from USD 122 million, which is why adjusted leverage fell from 8.08x at FY2025 to 2.58x on a last-twelve-months basis; leverage on reported EBITDA is not meaningful in any period.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation K1; calculation K5

Coverage. Cash interest on the only material borrowing is USD 38.75 million a year, so FY2025 adjusted EBITDA covered it 3.22x, while reported EBITDA was a deficit of 25.97 times cash interest. The 2026 quarterly reports state no cash interest paid, so cover for the last twelve months is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation K5

Cash-flow quality. Operating cash flow of USD 1,342 million in the nine months to September 2026 exceeded the net loss of USD 663 million because stock-based compensation of USD 855 million is non-cash and working capital released cash: deferred revenue added USD 533 million and receivables fell USD 410 million. Free cash flow was USD 1,254 million after capital expenditure of USD 83 million, so cash generation rests on customers paying in advance and on collections rather than on earnings. The change in deferred revenue was USD 136 million in the third quarter against USD 573 million a year earlier, so that source of funding slowed sharply.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K10

Liquidity. Cash and equivalents of USD 1,093 million exceed total debt of USD 1,009 million, a net cash position of USD 84 million on the method's narrow cash definition. Adding USD 5,145 million of short-term and long-term investments, cash and investments cover total debt 6.18 times. The filings describe no committed revolving facility, so there is no undrawn capacity to add, and share repurchases of USD 576 million were the only financing outflow in the nine months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation K2; calculation K3

Non-debt funding float. Deferred revenue of USD 7,040 million at 2026-09-30 is an interest-free obligation funded by payments already collected, and it dwarfs total debt of USD 1,009 million; the developer exchange liability to creators adds USD 444 million. These obligations are settled in virtual items and creator payouts rather than interest, so they matter for liquidity when bookings weaken, not for leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation K4

Legal costs and later events. The nine-month result includes USD 140 million of legal settlement expense, USD 49 million of it in the third quarter; these are cash payments owed to states, added back in the issuer's adjusted EBITDA but expensed in reported EBITDA. The quarterly report describes developments to 2026-10-29, including a notice from the Federal Trade Commission in October 2026, but states no amount, so no adjustment to net debt is made for any event after the balance sheet date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39

Definitions. Three EBITDA measures differ: reported EBITDA is negative, the issuer's adjusted EBITDA is USD 389 million for nine months 2026, and the covenant measure in the notes indenture is USD 900 million for the same period because it also adds back the growth in deferred revenue, a gap of USD 511 million to adjusted EBITDA. A reader comparing leverage across sources must name the measure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation K6
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is liquidity: cash and investments of USD 6,238 million are more than six times debt, the only sizeable maturity is the USD 1,000 million 2030 notes, and free cash flow of USD 1,254 million in nine months is positive, which points to a small refinancing need before 2030 whatever the EBITDA definition. The view that earnings cover is weak would be overturned if reported EBITDA turned positive, which needs operating profit to absorb the USD 855 million of stock-based compensation expensed in the nine months, or if bookings regained growth. It would be confirmed if bookings keep falling, third-quarter bookings being USD 225 million below a year earlier, and the quarterly change in deferred revenue stays near USD 136 million, which would cut operating cash flow and leave settlement and repurchase outflows to be met from the investment portfolio.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K7
### Limitations

Statements are shown in USD millions: annual figures are converted exactly from thousands, but fiscal-year Q4 figures are not reported separately and no 2025 quarterly report is in the set, so Q4 2025 and every 2024 quarter are not available as printed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

Reported EBITDA is built from the operating loss and depreciation and amortization because the issuer states none; interest income, other income and taxes are left out, in line with the issuer's own adjusted measure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation K5
Cash interest paid is stated for fiscal years only, so interest cover for the last twelve months and for interim dates is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12
The key-metric charts of the filings are not available as text, so user and engagement figures are limited to the sentences that state them.

## Gaps

Reported EBITDA is negative in every period, so total debt and net debt over reported EBITDA are not calculable for any period; this restricts every leverage statement to the issuer-adjusted measure, severity High, and the action is to name the measure whenever a leverage multiple is quoted.

Cash interest paid is stated only for the fiscal years in the annual report, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for the three interim last-twelve-months dates; severity Medium, and the action is to obtain cash interest paid from the 2026 filings or to use the fiscal-year multiples.

No 2025 quarterly report is in the set, so Q4 2025 is not printed and every 2024 quarter, including Q4 2024, is not available; year-on-year quarterly comparisons for the fourth quarter are not calculable; severity Medium, and the action is to supply the 2025 quarterly reports.

The undrawn committed facilities column of the liquidity table is not supplied for any period because the filings describe no committed facility; severity Low, and the action is to confirm with the company that none exists.

The amount of letters of credit at 2026-09-30 is not stated in the quarterly reports, which give only the USD 9.3 million of FY2025; severity Low, and the action is to obtain the figure from the company.

The legal rank of the 2030 notes and of the joint venture notes is not stated beyond the instrument names, so the debt stack is not stated and no secured or senior subtotal is built; severity Medium, and the action is to supply the indenture.

Lines printed as a dash in the filings, such as the legal settlement add-back for the 2025 comparatives, payments for business combinations in some columns and the foreign exchange effect for nine months 2026, are carried as not supplied rather than zero; severity Low, and the action is none beyond reading the filing.

Lines that appear in only the annual or only the quarterly cash flow statements, such as amortization of debt issuance costs, impairment and other items against other adjustments, are carried as not supplied in the columns where the filing does not print them; severity Low, and the action is none beyond reading the filing.
Cash taxes paid are stated for fiscal years only and the 2026 quarterly reports state no income taxes paid; severity Low, and the action is to use the income tax provision as an indication.
Operating metric series such as hours engaged by quarter and the 2025 quarterly daily active users are not available as text; severity Medium, and the action is to obtain the key-metric data.

The 2025 comparative Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations in the quarterly reports print totals one lower than their lines add to, from rounding in the issuer's table; the printed totals are used and the difference is noted; severity Low, and the action is none.

The fiscal-year FY2022 statements printed in the FY2024 annual report are not extracted because the credit snapshot window starts at FY2023; severity Low, and the action is to extract them if a longer history is wanted.
The headquarters lease floor area differs between the Q1 and Q2 reports and the Q3 report, with the same rent; severity Low, and the action is to quote rent and term only.

Items without a stated date after the balance sheet date, including the notice from the Federal Trade Commission in October 2026 and the settlement negotiations with states, carry no stated amount, so no pro forma net debt row is built; severity Medium, and the action is to read the next quarterly report.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Roblox is founder-controlled rather than sponsor-owned, so creditors depend on the founder's financial policy, which is cash-funded so far but unconstrained by any distribution limit the filings describe. Class B stock carries 56.94% of votes, and a USD 3.0 billion buyback authorization is three times the USD 1,000 million of notes.

Policy has not yet hurt creditors: no dividend has ever been paid, no debt was issued in 2026, and repurchases of USD 580 million in nine months 2026 were paid from cash and investments of USD 6.2 billion. The risks that could change this are state settlements, which cost USD 140 million over the same nine months with more claims pending, and an indenture that the filings summarise without any limit on distributions.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 105–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 51–53; calculation V1; calculation V5
### Key findings

Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, not High, because documented conduct toward creditors is neutral so far, while the structure lets one holder change policy without any outside check. No dividend has been paid, buybacks are funded from cash, and no controlling sponsor, sponsor fee, dividend recapitalisation, or amendment, waiver or exchange of the notes appears in the filings read; against that, distribution capacity, board independence and related-party dealings cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 196; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21

Voting control rests with the founder alone, so no outside holder can force a change of policy and a takeover is improbable. Class B stock carries 20 votes a share and is wholly owned by the founder and his affiliates; on share counts it was 56.94% of all votes at 2026-09-30, down from 58.74% at 2025-12-31 after the number of Class B shares fell in April 2026 for reasons the filings do not give. The company has elected out of Nevada's statute on business combinations with large holders, so its defences are the dual-class structure, a staggered board and a two-thirds vote for certain charter amendments. The notes' offer to repurchase at 101% of principal on a change of control therefore protects against an event the structure makes unlikely, and gives no check on the founder's own policy choices.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 105–107; 10-Q_2026-03-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation V1; calculation V2

Capital returns are funded from cash, but they are new and discretionary, and book equity is now a deficit. Roblox bought back no stock in FY2025; after a USD 3.0 billion authorization in May 2026 it repurchased USD 580 million by 2026-09-30, USD 380 million in the second quarter and USD 200 million in the third, and says it intends up to USD 1.0 billion in the first twelve months. Cash paid for repurchases was 42.92% of nine-month operating cash flow, and with the net loss it helped move total stockholders' equity from USD 375 million at 2025-12-31 to a deficit of USD 27 million. The program can be suspended at any time, and USD 2.4 billion of authority remains.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 151; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 136; calculation V5; calculation V6; calculation V7; calculation V16

The covenant package as the company describes it limits liens, debt and mergers and names no limit on dividends or repurchases, so distribution capacity is a gap rather than a finding. The company says the limits apply up to the greater of USD 4.0 billion and 3.5 times Consolidated EBITDA, states compliance at 2026-09-30, and prices the notes at par for 2026 and thereafter, so the notes can be refinanced without a premium. No willingness to extract is inferred from capacity; the documented distributions are the buybacks above.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 197

User-safety litigation is the main event risk and has already reached the income statement every quarter of 2026. Settlement expense was USD 57 million, USD 34 million and USD 49 million in the three quarters, USD 140 million in all, against an immaterial accrual at 2025-12-31. The number of states that had sued rose from seven at 2026-04-30 to ten at 2026-07-30, two California counties have also sued, six states have settled, and the Federal Trade Commission, Pennsylvania and Utah told the company in October 2026 that they are considering claims. Public-service campaigns, law-enforcement liaison staff, platform changes and liquidated damages under the settlements are not accrued and no loss estimate beyond the accrual is given, so USD 140 million is a floor.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 176; 10-Q_2026-03-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; calculation V11; calculation V12

Cash generation depends on advance payments from a thin paying base, so weaker bookings would reach liquidity before revenue. Users buy Robux upfront, payments are held in deferred revenue of USD 7,040 million at 2026-09-30 and most revenue is recognised over a paying user's estimated 27-month life, while only about 1.30% of daily active users pay. Bookings growth against the same quarter a year earlier slowed through 2026, from 43.41% in the first quarter to 8.28% in the second and a fall of 11.71% in the third, though nine-month bookings were still 9.15% higher, and the company says its safety changes have affected bookings and may continue to.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-03-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation V9; calculation V10; calculation V15

Platform dependence is a second-order risk that concentrates bookings in a few channels and titles. Apple and Google carried 44% of FY2025 revenue at fees of up to 30%, 51% of in-experience hours in December 2025 were spent in the top 50 experiences, and Apple, Google and an affiliate of Tencent are both named competitors and channel or joint-venture partners, so a policy or pricing change by any of them would reach bookings quickly. Developer exchange fees took 26.52% of nine-month revenue and the creator payout rate was raised twice, in September 2025 and June 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation V3; calculation V4

Management incentives reward bookings growth rather than cash margin and carry no cash cost. The founder's 2024 award was earned at twice target on cumulative bookings and an Adjusted EBITDA measure that the company says correlates to the covenant measure; most of it has vested and the remainder vests in four quarterly instalments that began in the second quarter of 2026. The Chief Financial Officer changed between the FY2024 and FY2025 reports after the prior officer gave notice in August 2024.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 185; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 199; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; calculation V13

Fixed commitments outside debt are growing. Hosting agreements signed in June 2026 total USD 845 million over three annual periods from 2026-07-01, and headquarters leases signed in January 2026 add about USD 403 million of base rent over about 13 years, roughly USD 31 million a year once occupied. Both come on top of the USD 1,000 million bullet due 2030-05-01, and the filings do not print the three hosting amounts individually.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation V8; calculation V14

Subsidiary-level claims are small. An affiliate of Tencent Holdings holds 49% of Roblox China Holding Corp. and USD 15 million of its notes, now due 2028-05-10 and convertible by the lenders into voting shares of that subsidiary; Roblox's own USD 15 million of the same notes is eliminated on consolidation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 31
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern about financial policy is that nothing in the record yet shows creditors losing from it: no controlling sponsor is named, no dividend has ever been paid, repurchases took 42.92% of nine-month operating cash flow, cash and investments of USD 6.2 billion are well above the USD 1,000 million of notes, the company states compliance with its covenants, and no amendment, waiver or exchange is described. The view would soften further if the indenture proved to restrict distributions tightly. It would harden if repurchases ran above operating cash flow or above the USD 1.0 billion first-year intention, if any distribution were debt-funded, if new debt or liens were put in place under the USD 4.0 billion basket, if settlement costs rose well above USD 140 million, or if bookings kept falling from the USD 1,697 million of the third quarter while buybacks continued.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation V6
### Limitations

- The finding that distribution capacity is unmeasured rests on the company's own summary of the notes covenants; if the indenture holds a restricted-payments covenant the risk level would fall, and if its debt and lien baskets are wide it would rise.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 197

- The 56.94% vote share counts Class B stock only, so the founder's total voting power may be understated by his Class A shares and awards, and board independence and related-party dealings are not established; none of this changes majority control, but it would change the Medium rating if related-party payments proved material.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 196; calculation V1

- The second-quarter business acquisition is not named or described, so the view that acquisition appetite is low rests on USD 6 million of cash and USD 17 million of stock, restricted stock units and cash consideration payable; a larger or debt-funded purchase would change the capital-allocation view.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12
- The litigation notes give no loss estimate beyond amounts accrued, so the legal-cost finding is a floor; further settlements would reduce the cash available for repurchases and debt service.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25

- The hosting purchase commitments are printed as a total and a range that do not reconcile, so the finding on fixed commitments could be out by about USD 5 million in one annual period; the lease rent is a total over the term, not a schedule.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; calculation V14

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No debt was issued, repaid or refinanced by Roblox Corporation in 2026; the nine-month cash flow statement shows no debt proceeds or repayments. The only material borrowing remains the USD 1,000 million 3.875% unsecured senior notes due 2030-05-01, issued on 2021-10-29 for net proceeds of about USD 988 million that the company said it intended to use for general corporate purposes, including working capital, capital expenditures, share repurchases and acquisitions. The notes are redeemable at par for 2026 and thereafter, and holders may require repurchase at 101% of principal on a change of control triggering event. The only change to any debt in 2026 was the two-year extension, in the first quarter, of the USD 30 million joint venture notes of Roblox China Holding Corp. to 2028-05-10, which Roblox and an affiliate of Tencent funded equally.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 51

The 2026 transactions are equity, lease and purchase decisions. In the second quarter Roblox issued 993 thousand shares of common stock valued at USD 12 million in the acquisition of a business whose target and terms are not described; the six-month cash flow shows USD 6 million of cash paid and USD 17 million of stock, restricted stock units and cash consideration payable. In May 2026 the board authorized repurchases of up to USD 3.0 billion, and USD 580 million had been bought by 2026-09-30. On 2026-01-30 the company executed leases for two more headquarters buildings with about USD 403 million of incremental base rent over about 13 years, and in June 2026 it signed hosting agreements for USD 845 million over three annual periods. No acquisition financing, sponsor transaction or new borrowing is described.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 26

## Request

Fundamental credit analysis for Roblox Corp (Roblox Corporation, ticker RBLX; issuer id rblx-1315098), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The module combines the five supplied filings with the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules into the business, financial, governance and downside view a creditor needs, and states every gap.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Roblox's credit profile rests on liquidity, not earnings: USD 6.2 billion of cash and investments covers total debt of USD 1,009 million 6.18 times, but reported EBITDA is negative and cash flow depends on advance payments that slowed sharply in the third quarter.

Repayment risk before the 2030 maturity is therefore low. The primary downside is a slow erosion: average daily paying users fell 21.74% year on year in the third quarter, bookings fell 11.71%, and costs and legal settlements keep rising while revenue still benefits from earlier advance sales.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation W1; calculation W6; calculation W7
### Key findings

Liquidity is the decisive credit support and is large against the cash claims the filings identify. Cash and investments were USD 6.2 billion at 2026-09-30 against total debt of USD 1,009 million, the only maturities are USD 15 million in 2028 and USD 1,000 million in 2030, and remaining debt service is USD 19 million in 2026 and USD 39 million a year for 2027 to 2029. Treasury, agency and money market holdings are 73.92% of the debt securities and a 100 bp rise in rates would cut their fair value by about USD 62 million, so the cushion is liquid and short in duration. The fixed calls identified through 2030, being hosting, debt service and the 2030 principal, total USD 1,981 million and are covered 3.15 times by cash and investments before any operating cash flow, and adding lease liabilities, new headquarters rent, creator payables and settlement expense to total debt and hosting gives USD 3,742 million, still covered 1.67 times. Deferred revenue, which is settled in virtual items, and the discretionary repurchase authority are left out of that sum.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 57; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation W1; calculation W3; calculation W4; calculation W25

Earnings do not carry the debt. Reported EBITDA was a loss of USD 613 million in nine months 2026 and is negative in every period covered, and the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 389 million adds back USD 855 million of stock-based compensation, a real cost to holders. Total debt is 2.58 times last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, a multiple that is not comparable with conventional leverage, so creditors are repaid from the liquidity cushion and cash receipts rather than from earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation W16

Free cash flow is positive but rests on working capital, and it weakened in the third quarter. Free cash flow was USD 1,254 million in nine months 2026 against USD 1,046 million a year earlier, yet 72.01% of it came from changes in operating assets and liabilities, mainly USD 533 million of deferred revenue growth and USD 410 million from lower receivables. Derived third-quarter free cash flow was USD 364 million against USD 442 million a year earlier, and operating cash flow USD 395 million against USD 546 million, as the quarterly increase in deferred revenue fell to USD 136 million from USD 573 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation W13; calculation W14

Revenue is more durable than bookings, but only for as long as deferred sales last, and bookings are now falling. Revenue rose 15.59% in the third quarter while bookings fell 11.71%, because revenue is recognized over a paying user's estimated 27 months and 73.61% of nine-month revenue came from the current deferred balance held at the start of the year. The company attributes the bookings fall to fewer paying users, a 21.74% drop, and separately says that mandatory age checks since January 2026 led to an unexpected decline in the rate of growth; it does not state how much of the payer fall the age checks explain. Revenue will fall behind bookings with a lag, and the USD 7,040 million deferred balance cushions revenue, not cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation W5; calculation W6; calculation W7; calculation W8; calculation W9

Costs are growing faster than they can be cut, so operating leverage turns against creditors if bookings keep falling. Total costs rose 12.02% in the third quarter against a fall in bookings, the company says it plans to raise research, general and marketing spending, and USD 845 million of hosting is committed. Only developer exchange fees, 26.52% of nine-month revenue, have flexed with bookings, falling 6% in the quarter, and on an indicative estimate third-quarter bookings were only 15.09% above the level that covers cash operating costs before working capital.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation W10; calculation W18

Legal and regulatory pressure is the main cause of downside and has no stated ceiling. Settlement expense was USD 140 million in nine months 2026, ten states and two counties have sued, the Federal Trade Commission and two states are considering claims, and the 2025 annual report states that fines can reach 6% of annual global revenue under the EU Digital Services Act and 10% under the UK Online Safety Act, with a Netherlands investigation of Roblox announced in January 2026. Whether any such fine is likely is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial policy is the swing factor for creditors and sits with one holder. The founder controls 56.94% of votes through Class B stock, the board authorized USD 3.0 billion of repurchases of which USD 580 million was spent in nine months 2026, total stockholders' equity moved from USD 375 million to a deficit of USD 27 million, and the company's description of the notes covenants names no limit on distributions. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium, and this analysis agrees because documented conduct toward creditors is neutral so far.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation W17

Refinancing is not a near-term test, but market access cannot be shown. The notes are unsecured, callable at par for 2026 and thereafter, and due on 2030-05-01, with no rating and no market quote supplied. Their estimated fair value fell to 91.7% of principal at 2026-09-30 from 95.8% at 2025-12-31, and the company says the value moves with interest rates and other factors, so the filings do not say whether the fall reflects credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation W21
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that distress is implausible for years on the numbers reported: revenue rose 28.97% in nine months 2026, the operating loss narrowed to 17.98% of revenue from 25.12%, adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.68% from 3.51%, free cash flow of USD 1,254 million exceeded repurchases and settlements together, capital expenditure was only 1.85% of revenue, and nine-month bookings were still 9.15% higher. The company also describes the age-check effect as unexpected and tied to a platform change, which could prove a one-off step rather than a trend. The view would improve if bookings returned to growth and paying users recovered, and it would worsen if bookings fell again in the fourth quarter, the strongest seasonal quarter, with deferred revenue growth below USD 136 million, if repurchases exceeded free cash flow, if settlements rose well above USD 140 million, or if any distribution were debt-funded.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation W5; calculation W6; calculation W10; calculation W11; calculation W15
### Limitations

- The paying-user decline is computed from counts that the company gives only as approximate figures to the nearest tenth of a million, so the 21.74% fall could lie between 17.78% and 25.53%; a smaller true fall would weaken the conclusion that fewer payers explain the bookings decline.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation W7

- Third-quarter operating and free cash flow are derived by subtracting six-month from nine-month amounts that are each rounded to millions, so the finding that cash generation weakened in the quarter is reliable in direction but not in exact size.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation W13

- The filings state no outlook figure and no peer financials are supplied, so the twelve to twenty-four month outlook and the comparison of the business profile with typical leveraged-credit issuers rest on the company's own reported trends; a peer set with stronger bookings would make the third-quarter fall look company-specific rather than structural.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The break-even bookings level is an indicative estimate that treats total costs less stock-based compensation and depreciation as cash costs and ignores working capital timing, so the 15.09% cushion could be wider or narrower in practice.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation W18

- Legal rank, guarantees and the covenant definitions of the notes are not in the filings, so the refinancing finding assumes the notes stand as unsecured obligations of the parent with no claims ranking ahead except the small subsidiary notes; a structurally senior claim would change the ranking of creditors but not the repayment capacity shown here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The five main strengths are these. Liquidity is large, with cash and investments of USD 6,238 million against total debt of USD 1,009 million, no maturity before 2028 and an unsecured bullet in 2030, so repayment does not depend on earnings. Advance payments give revenue visibility, with deferred revenue of USD 7,040 million and 73.61% of nine-month revenue already deferred at the start of the year. Scale and the creator network support engagement, with 138 million average daily users in the third quarter and more than 45,000 creators in the Developer Exchange Program. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditure of USD 83 million in nine months 2026, so free cash flow of USD 1,254 million does not need reinvestment to hold the platform. Developer payouts flex with bookings, falling 6% in the third quarter as bookings fell, which gives one real cost lever.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation W1; calculation W8; calculation W15

The five main weaknesses are these. Bookings and payers are falling, with third-quarter bookings down 11.71% and average daily paying users down 21.74%, which moves the first cash lever of the business. Earnings are negative, with reported EBITDA a loss of USD 613 million in nine months 2026 and adjusted EBITDA dependent on a USD 855 million stock-based compensation add-back. Cash flow leans on working capital, which was 72.01% of free cash flow, and the deferred revenue float is growing more slowly. Legal and regulatory exposure is open-ended, with USD 140 million expensed, ten states and two counties suing and no loss estimate beyond the accrual. Financial policy is concentrated in the founder, who controls 56.94% of votes, with a USD 3.0 billion repurchase authorization, a stockholders' deficit of USD 27 million and no distribution limit described.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rblx.htm.jsonl, page 46; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation W6; calculation W7; calculation W14

### Company description

Roblox runs a single-segment immersive gaming and creation platform made of a client application, a free creation toolset and cloud infrastructure. Creators build experiences and users buy the virtual currency Robux to enhance them, either one-time or through the Premium subscription. Users on the platform averaged 138 million a day in the third quarter of 2026, of whom about 1.8 million paid, and 54% of nine-month revenue came from the United States, with 57% from the United States and Canada, 21% from Europe, 12% from Asia-Pacific and 10% from the rest of the world. Creators earned USD 1,503.1 million of Developer Exchange payouts in FY2025 against USD 922.8 million in FY2024, and more than 45,000 creators were registered in the program at 2026-09-30 against more than 35,500 at 2025-12-31.

The credit linkage runs through cash timing. Payment is taken upfront for substantially all bookings, recorded in deferred revenue and recognized over the estimated lifetime of a paying user, which gives visibility of revenue and a cash float of USD 7,040 million, and it also means the business can show growing revenue after demand has slowed. The user base includes many children, which the company names as a reputational risk and which exposes it to online-safety law, and 44% of FY2025 revenue passed through two app stores. Operating history is one of losses: net losses attributable to common stockholders were USD 1,065.1 million in FY2025, USD 935.4 million in FY2024 and USD 1,151.9 million in FY2023, with an accumulated deficit of USD 5,060.7 million at 2025-12-31. The only structural changes in 2026 are small: one acquisition of a business in the second quarter, two more headquarters buildings leased, and a USD 3.0 billion repurchase authorization.

### Ownership and group structure

Roblox is a listed, founder-led and founder-controlled company with no sponsor named: the founder and his affiliates own all Class B stock, which carries 20 votes a share and was 56.94% of all votes at 2026-09-30 on share counts, down from 58.74% at 2025-12-31. The group has one consolidated subsidiary with a minority, Roblox China Holding Corp., in which Roblox holds 51% of the voting shares and an affiliate of Tencent Holdings holds 49%; it has issued USD 30 million of notes, half held by that affiliate, due 2028-05-10, which are the only debt that sits below the parent. The filings define no restricted or unrestricted group and name no guarantor of the 2030 notes, so structural seniority of subsidiary debt is limited to USD 15 million.

For financial policy, Business & governance finds no dividend ever paid, USD 580 million of repurchases in nine months 2026 funded from cash, a USD 3.0 billion authorization, founder control that leaves distribution policy to one holder, and an indenture whose distribution limits cannot be read. The credit implication is policy risk, not structural subordination risk: creditors depend on the founder's choices, and the one documented distribution, buybacks, has been covered by operating cash flow.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is driven by volume of users, the number who pay and spend per payer. Average daily users were 127 million in FY2025 against 82.9 million in FY2024, 132 million, 123 million and 138 million in the three 2026 quarters, and about 1.8 million paid in the third quarter. Bookings rose 55.37% in FY2025 and 9.15% in nine months 2026, but quarterly growth slowed from 43.41% in the first quarter to 8.28% in the second and a fall of 11.71% in the third, and the third-quarter fall was driven by average daily paying users dropping to about 1.8 million from about 2.3 million. Average daily bookings per paying user were USD 9.98 in the third quarter against USD 10.42 in the second, and bookings per daily user USD 0.13.

Revenue is transactional and discretionary, with a subscription element, concentrated in channel and title, and sensitive to regulation. The company sets the creator payout rate in its sole discretion and has used that power to give value back: it raised the payout per earned Robux by 8.5% in September 2025 and the Developer Exchange rate by 42% for eligible adult US spend in June 2026, and it offers more Robux through lower-fee payment channels, so pricing power over creators and payers is limited and used defensively. The credit mechanism is that bookings, not revenue, drive cash; revenue is smoothed by deferral, durable items were 90% of virtual item revenue in nine months 2026, and the deferred balance gives revenue visibility of about twelve months, with USD 4,781 million of it classified as current and a tail to roughly 27 months.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of revenue was 20% of nine-month revenue, developer exchange fees 27%, infrastructure and trust & safety 24%, research and development 28%, general and administrative 14% and sales and marketing 5%, so total costs were 118% of revenue against 125% a year earlier. Developer exchange fees follow bookings and fell in the third quarter; cost of revenue follows revenue because payment processing fees are expensed over the same period as the related revenue; infrastructure, safety, research and general costs are driven by headcount, hosting and legal activity, and the company says it expects to raise research, general and marketing spending and to increase infrastructure investment over the long term. Total costs rose 21.61% in nine months 2026 against revenue growth of 28.97%, and 12.02% in the third quarter against revenue growth of 15.59% and a fall in bookings.

Margins can be defended against a modest fall in volume because developer payouts flex, but not against a sustained one, because the headcount and hosting base, including USD 845 million of hosting commitments over three annual periods and about USD 403 million of new headquarters rent, does not flex. The reported operating loss was 17.98% of revenue in nine months 2026 against 25.12%, an improvement driven by revenue recognized from earlier bookings rather than by lower costs, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.68% against 3.51%. The credit implication is that margin gains are tied to deferred revenue release, and a bookings decline would first show in cash flow and then in revenue and margin over the following twelve to 27 months of the deferral period.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was USD 83 million in nine months 2026 against USD 143 million, 1.85% of revenue, although USD 125 million of property additions sat in payables and accruals against USD 48 million a year earlier, so cash capital spending is lagging accruals. Leases are operating leases with USD 901 million of liabilities on the balance sheet at 2026-09-30, and the two new headquarters buildings add about USD 403 million of rent over about 13 years from a start that had not yet occurred. Interest paid is small at USD 38.75 million a year, income taxes are immaterial at USD 4 million of provision in nine months 2026 with a full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, and no restructuring or integration cash cost is described in the filings read.

Free cash flow was 3.22 times adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, which is a sign that cash conversion is flattered by working capital rather than a measure of operating strength: without the USD 903 million inflow from operating assets and liabilities, free cash flow would have been USD 351 million. Bookings are typically highest in the fourth quarter, and the derived fourth quarter of 2025 supplied 40.44% of FY2025 covenant EBITDA, a measure that adds deferred revenue growth; for nine months 2026 it was USD 900 million against USD 1,029 million a year earlier. The conclusion is that cash generation is durable while bookings grow and fragile if they stall, and it is sufficient to service debt either way.

### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is high. The company names global technology, entertainment, gaming and online content companies, including Apple, Google, Microsoft, Tencent, Netflix, YouTube and Epic Games, as competitors for user attention and creators, and the evidence of effect is the fall in paying users in the third quarter and the dip in average daily users in the second. The mechanism is that engagement and payer retention, not price, set bookings, and the implication is that bookings can move faster than costs.

Buyer power is high at the user and creator level and low at the payer level. Users play for free, only about 1.30% of daily users pay, and the company has raised creator payouts twice, in September 2025 and June 2026, which indicates that creator retention has a cost; the mechanism is cost creep in developer exchange fees and a bookings base that depends on a small payer group. Supplier power is meaningful: Apple and Google take up to 30% of purchases on 44% of FY2025 revenue and can change terms, hosting providers hold USD 845 million of commitments, and payment processors set fees that the company manages through differential pricing. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because scale in creators and infrastructure and trust and safety spending of 24% of revenue raise the cost of entry, while the threat of substitutes is high because the same child and teen time can go to other entertainment.

### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are a primary credit driver and are covered here; economic, social and technological factors matter only where they connect to the same mechanism. Regulatory: the 2025 annual report lists the Digital Services Act, the UK Online Safety Act, Australia's minimum-age law, the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act amendments with a compliance date of 2026-04-22, state app-store and minor-purchase laws, and a possible loss of liability protections; compliance has already required mandatory age checks that, by the company's own account, led to an unexpected decline in the rate of growth. Social: the user base includes many children, so safety is a condition of the business, and it has produced state lawsuits and settlements costing USD 140 million in nine months 2026. Economic: the company cites inflation and weaker consumer spending as risks to discretionary spending by users, which reaches bookings. Technological: dependence on operating systems and app stores, and investment in age-check and moderation technology, raise cost and constrain growth. The credit effect is that regulation can change the user base and the cost base at the same time, a change that earnings cannot absorb but liquidity can.

### SWOT analysis

Strengths in credit terms are liquidity of USD 6,238 million against debt of USD 1,009 million, advance payments and a USD 7,040 million deferred balance, low capital intensity, and a creator network whose registered Developer Exchange creators grew 26.76% in nine months. Weaknesses are negative reported EBITDA, a thin payer base, a cost base that is rising ahead of bookings, and concentration of channel and titles. The only opportunities that could improve credit quality are a return of bookings growth as users adapt to age checks, higher engagement among older audiences through the company's novel-game expansion, and lower payment costs from a mix shift to cheaper channels. The threats that could weaken credit quality are further regulatory action and fines, more state settlements, a change in app-store terms, and repurchases that outpace cash flow.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are liquidity, advance payments, low capital intensity and a single unsecured bullet maturity in 2030. The main constraints are negative reported EBITDA, dependence on working capital for free cash flow, a bookings and payer decline, open-ended legal and regulatory cost, and founder-controlled financial policy. The trend is mixed: revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow improved over nine months 2026, while the forward indicators, bookings, paying users, the quarterly change in deferred revenue and covenant earnings, which fell 45.63% in the third quarter, deteriorated. The datapoints still missing are a management outlook, ratings, market prices, the indenture, peer figures and the cost of unaccrued settlement commitments.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The company states no outlook figure, so the next twelve to twenty-four months are read from reported trends. The fourth quarter is seasonally the strongest for bookings, so it is the next test of whether the third-quarter fall was a step or a trend; the company says it expects to continue safety changes in response to regulation, that safety changes have impacted and may continue to impact bookings, that it intends up to USD 1.0 billion of repurchases in the first twelve months of the program, and that settlement talks with other states continue. Company-specific tailwinds are lower payment costs from channel mix, an expanding creator base and the revenue release from the deferred balance; headwinds are age-check friction, litigation, rising hosting and personnel costs, and app-store fees. Over three to five years the 2030 maturity is the only debt event, and its repayment depends on liquidity that is currently several times debt rather than on earnings. Sector tailwinds and headwinds are not evidenced beyond the company's own risk factors and no peer data is supplied.

### Downside scenario

The most credible issuer-specific downside begins with a regulatory or enforcement event that removes more users or payers than the age-check change did, such as a finding under the Digital Services Act, an action by the Federal Trade Commission, or a further wave of state measures. The first operational break is a second consecutive fall in bookings: third-quarter bookings of USD 1,697 million were USD 136 million above the USD 1,561 million at which deferred revenue would stop growing at the third-quarter revenue level, so a further fall of 8.01% would end the float. Financial transmission follows in order: operating cash flow loses the deferred revenue inflow, which was USD 533 million in nine months 2026; revenue keeps rising for several quarters from the USD 7,040 million deferred balance, so reported margins stay flattered; costs of USD 1,855 million in the third quarter, hosting commitments and legal settlements do not fall; and free cash flow shrinks from USD 364 million in the quarter toward zero.

The liquidity and refinancing consequence is limited in the near term: on an indicative basis bookings of USD 1,441 million, 15.09% below the third quarter, would leave cash operating costs just covered before working capital, and even at zero operating cash flow cash and investments of USD 6,238 million would cover the identified fixed calls of USD 1,981 million more than three times. Management levers are suspending the repurchase program, which may be suspended at any time and has USD 2.4 billion of authority left, slowing hiring and infrastructure, and stopping further buybacks before any borrowing. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over twelve to twenty-four months; the observable triggers are a second quarter of falling bookings, a quarterly deferred revenue change below USD 136 million, free cash flow below USD 364 million, settlement expense above USD 140 million, and repurchases above free cash flow. No default is assumed.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Roblox presents a business profile that is large and broad by geography but concentrated by channel, title and paying users, supported by liquidity of USD 6,238 million and advance payments, but credit quality is constrained by negative reported EBITDA, a falling bookings and payer base, open-ended legal and regulatory cost, and policy set by one holder. Cash-flow durability appears adequate while bookings hold and weak if they keep falling, because free cash flow leans on working capital. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on liquidity, which is several times the debt, not on market access, which the filings do not evidence. The primary downside path is regulation-driven loss of paying users that cuts bookings, ends the deferred revenue float and leaves a rising cost base and legal cost to be met from the cash cushion over several years. Further analysis would require a management outlook, the indenture, ratings and market prices, peer financials and fourth-quarter results. Top risk: loss of paying users and bookings from user-safety regulation.
